dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "17 annual-plan (term_days=365) records for DLR-104 and DLR-219 were posted on 31 May, with effective dates 1–28 May, totaling $1,506.29."
"DLR-104 batch DF-00020 had 8/8 rows accepted, 0 duplicate source events, and $723.42 cash = $723.42 ledger. DLR-219 batch DF-00040 had 9/9 accepted, 0 duplicates, and $782.87 cash = $782.87 ledger."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "Their effective_event_date runs from 1 May to 28 May, while all were posted on 31 May."
"The timing is systematic and contract/process-driven rather than an unexplained failure."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "The email is treated as corroboration because the same behavior is independently visible in the data."
"The supplied files do not identify which dealer ID corresponds to each dealer name in the email, nor do they provide a direct financial-ledger duplicate check beyond the import reconciliation."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "A ledger-level one-to-one check would change the decision if any recharge_id or amount appeared more than once in revenue recognition."
"If any ID is duplicated, missing, or has an amount mismatch, immediately escalate the affected records for possible duplicate revenue or reporting-control failure."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "No material issue; do not escalate as duplicate revenue or manipulated reporting."
"Run a read-only reconciliation of the 17 affected recharge_id and amount_usd records..."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Manipulated reporting: Rejected." The evidence supports a documented benign posting process and successful reconciliation, but does not by itself rule out all forms of reporting manipulation.

"The timing is systematic and contract/process-driven rather than an unexplained failure." This is plausible and well supported, but the evidence covers only two dealers and does not fully exclude a separate event-time pipeline defect.

"If every ID maps one-to-one and the amounts reconcile, keep the current no-escalation decision." This is operationally reasonable, but the proposed check largely repeats checks already reported as complete and does not address downstream analytics distortion.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission considered duplicate revenue, manipulated reporting, and a pipeline defect, but missed the strongest residual interpretation: the postings may be financially benign while still creating a material event-time defect for retention, month-end, or cohort analytics. The downstream safeguard should use effective_event_date rather than posted_at.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly separate financial-control reconciliation from analytical validity: retain the no-escalation conclusion if duplicate cash and entitlement checks reconcile, but require downstream renewal and retention analytics to use effective_event_date and document the posting-time quirk.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South CareDesk tickets fell from 175 in January to 104 in June, while control regions were broadly flat: E 101→102, N 168→170, W 176→169."
"NovaIVR generated 2,709 South sessions, with 650 ending at `authenticate`; that is 24.0% of NOVA sessions, and these sessions have no verified customer case in the CareDesk view."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The pilot email says sessions ending before authentication are monitored in the technical pilot report rather than CareDesk because no verified customer context exists."
"The recording process changed, so the case-count denominator changed with it."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "While genuine deflection occurred for routine queries (29.1% balance checks, 21.3% pack info), unresolved technical issues went unrecorded."
"I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Decision: Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet; keep the South pilot at its current scope while measuring contacts like-for-like."
"It is cheap and fully reversible: it writes no customer record, changes no routing, and its output can be discarded."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The single next action is one targeted, read-only 7-day repeat-contact/callback query reconciled to all NOVA sessions."
"What written pass threshold and observation window govern pilot-to-national expansion?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "My inference is that complaint volume was suppressed by channel filtering" is directionally plausible and consistent with the measurement failure, but the cited authentication-stage abandonment does not establish that the affected sessions were complaints or that their issues remained unresolved.

"Telemetry in service_events.csv confirms ongoing customer impact" overstates what service-event counts establish: they show exposure or operational incidents, not necessarily customer dissatisfaction, complaint incidence, or failed resolution.

"Under NOVA-S1, only 90 of 2,709 sessions reached `case_create`" is accurately reported, but interpreting the difference from legacy as a changed recording process should also account for differences in journey mix and the fact that legacy and NOVA cohorts may not be directly comparable.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission appropriately considers genuine routine-query deflection, but it misses or underdevelops the strongest benign alternative: authentication abandonment may include sessions that were resolved through another route or involved no complaint at all. Service-event exposure likewise does not map one-for-one to complaints. Journey linkage or sampled call listening is needed to distinguish missing capture from legitimate non-case outcomes.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add end-to-end validation of a sampled set of authentication failures and abandonments, linked where possible to repeat contacts, callbacks, eventual cases, and resolution outcomes. This would test whether the missing CareDesk cases represent unresolved friction rather than relying primarily on repeat-contact rates.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `inverter_events.csv`, rows 1–4, and names the specific fields supporting dates, inverter IDs, durations, impact, cleared status, event, and severity.
It distinguishes observations such as “All 4 rows have `impact_mw=0` and `cleared=yes`” from the inference that escalation is not warranted.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly avoids treating the single `COMM_LINK_WARN` label as proof of equipment failure: “Labels alone do not establish failure.”

It considers export incompleteness and proposes checking the raw database “without status filters,” but it does not triangulate against an independent operational channel or test the communications-warning mechanism directly.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It explicitly notes that “constant fields cannot distinguish affected from healthy units.”
It identifies the missing unfiltered plant baseline and extraction parameters, and limits its conclusion to the supplied extract: “if the 4 rows represent the entire dataset, conclude the review.”

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommended action is proportionate and read-only: “conduct a single read-only completeness verification.”
The proposed check is decision-relevant because uncleared faults or nonzero impacts would change the escalation decision, while avoiding unsupported equipment intervention.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion—“Do not escalate any event from this file”—fits the observed zero impact, cleared status, short durations, and dispersed one-per-inverter pattern.
It appropriately stops after a minimal completeness check rather than searching for a plant-failure narrative.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Low-severity” is slightly overstated: three events are labeled `info`, but the remaining event is a `warning`; the evidence supports low observed operational impact, not necessarily low severity in every operational sense.
“The four observed events represent isolated” is an inference from four distinct inverters and dates, not a directly established plant-wide fact.

“Escalate immediately” if unfiltered records show uncleared faults or nonzero losses is somewhat broad; those records would warrant prompt validation and triage, though the proposed direction is operationally reasonable.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The `COMM_LINK_WARN` could represent a transient communications interruption rather than an equipment problem. The extract cannot distinguish that mechanism or prove plant-wide completeness, but the zero `impact_mw`, cleared status, brief durations, and absence of repeated inverter IDs provide no basis for equipment escalation. The analyst’s recognized completeness gap is the most consequential alternative explanation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Perform the proposed unfiltered completeness check and report its result, including extraction filters and any uncleared or nonzero-impact records; if the export is complete, stop without pursuing a mechanism story.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission explicitly traces the 31.6% calculation to `dispatch_blocks.csv` and `AI_Pilot_Impact_Note.md`: “(662,444.09 - 453,085.88) / 662,444.09 = 31.6%.”
It identifies the same-day fields and calculation: “`base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, `dsm_rate_rs_kwh`, `schedule_source`; 96 blocks.”
It distinguishes multiple deviation metrics and gives their formulas, including block-level absolute deviation and absolute net daily imbalance.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission correctly identifies that the headline comparison uses two dates and notes that 28 May is the highest of eight daily penalties.

It constructs the required same-day modeled counterfactual: “Applying the documented banded penalty to `base_schedule_mw` against the same actual generation gives about Rs 549,664, versus Rs 453,086 submitted.”
It tests plausible alternative explanations, including day-to-day baseline variability, selection and timing, and the distinction between DSM penalty and total commercial value.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: It clearly separates observation from causal inference: “neither estimate establishes a general causal effect.”
It appropriately labels the same-day result “descriptive/model-based evidence for that day, not causal proof.”
It identifies decision-changing unknowns, including pre-outcome selection, immutable timestamps, replication across matched days, and complete net settlement data.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation is proportionate: “maintain the pilot at current scope and run the read-only shadow calculation; keep national expansion on hold.”
The proposed prospective test is discriminating and operationally relevant: “pre-registered matched high-wind stow days” with immutable timestamps and net commercial settlement.
The action preserves legitimate operational constraints and avoids unsupported expansion while retaining the possibility of pilot value.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion accurately preserves the smaller favorable result rather than rejecting the pilot entirely: “the stronger same-day modeled estimate is about 17.6%.”
It correctly scopes 31.6% as “valid arithmetic for two different days” but not as a causal estimate.
It reaches the best-supported decision: insufficient evidence for expansion, with further validation warranted.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that the proposed shadow-validation step is “completely reversible” and that “data can be discarded” is an operational assertion not directly established by the cited files, though it does not materially affect the analytical conclusion.

The phrase “the stronger same-day modeled estimate” could be read as stronger evidence rather than merely a better-controlled descriptive comparison; the surrounding caveats largely prevent that misreading.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The pilot may have produced a genuine positive operational effect on 29 May, reflected in the modeled 17.6% penalty reduction, while the 31.6% cross-day result may also be directionally favorable. However, day selection, weather/event severity, and the lack of replicated pre-specified comparisons prevent attributing either result generally or causally to the AI pilot.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain immutable pre-submission timestamps and run a pre-registered matched-day validation that reproduces the base-versus-submitted calculation across multiple high-wind events while reconciling DSM penalties, energy revenue, and pilot costs.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Schema omits system/version/date/ruling authority."
"Declaration: P1001 declared with 90211000."
"Helios 90211090 is commercial ERP data."
"Neither proves Swiss classification."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"‘Any differing string proves an error’: rejected because the Swiss reference lists 90211000 and warns Swiss/EU strings need not match."
"‘Helios master data supersedes local declaration filings’: rejected because Helios is commercial data without customs-ruling authority."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "closure needs Tares/ruling confirmation."
"Therefore the unresolved question is: what Swiss code was legally effective on 4 November 2025?"
"Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive"

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "canonical-schema-v0.3.md cannot store jurisdiction, version, or date, so whole-string comparison cannot establish broker error."
"Helios ... is commercial data, not legal authority."
"Tune the control by incorporating HS6 root matching and jurisdiction metadata rather than penalizing valid filings."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares or ruling confirmation."
"Verification, not escalation, is proportionate."
"This preserves both options while testing the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Correct codes from different editions appear as mismatches without discrepancy" is plausible but not demonstrated with a specific edition comparison in the submission.
"Binding classification requires official customs rulings" is stated broadly without identifying the applicable legal source or distinguishing a ruling from the effective Tares entry.
"No record contradicts 90211000" is appropriately bounded to the reviewed records, but the submission does not enumerate all records searched or establish completeness.

The proposed statement that an invoice-value mismatch would trigger review is not explained sufficiently; the submission identifies CHF 126,900 but does not specify the relevant valuation rule or expected broker calculation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss code legally effective on 2025-11-04 could differ from both 90211000 and the Helios suffix, meaning the declaration may still contain a genuine classification error. The submission appropriately leaves this possibility open and makes Tares or ruling confirmation the decisive test.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Cite the exact effective Tares entry or ruling, including jurisdiction, version and date, and explain the legal status of that source relative to the declaration and ERP data.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "IE-2025-000411 declares P1006 with Preference=Yes, United States origin, 0.0% duty, and 90211090."
"The only Irish-origin register entry supplied for P1006 is SUP-02, valid 2025-01-01 to 2025-07-31 and marked ‘Expired in register’; the shipment date is 2025-09-18."
"The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Preference indicator alone validates preferential treatment’: rejected because preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration"
"‘Commercial manufacturing country in commercial_invoice.pdf disproves preference’: rejected because manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preferential origin"
"‘The shipment should be flagged for fraud’: rejected because absence of a supplier declaration ... represents unverified documentation, not intentional misdeclaration."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The claim is unsupported by packet evidence, but not disproved."
"valid supplier declarations may exist in procurement archives."
"absence from the register does not prove that no document exists outside it."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "none identifies the supplier route supporting preference."
"Automated check in `review_note.txt` flagged missing ClearView links."
"A supplier-linked declaration and applicable rule is the decision-changing proof."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold the preference claim pending supplier-specific proof, request the declaration and governing rule from Procurement/Customs"
"do not clear it as preferential until verified."
"this hold is reversible and no duty change should be assumed until tariff treatment is confirmed."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that "preferential origin requires an active, linked supplier declaration" is presented as a legal requirement, but the submission cites only internal workshop, register and review materials rather than the governing preferential-origin rule; acceptable evidence requirements may depend on the applicable trade arrangement and customs procedure.

The statement that a "valid declaration flips decision to clear as preferential" is too categorical because a supplier declaration alone may not establish preferential origin without confirming the applicable rule, product qualification, shipment linkage and other required evidence.

The statement that SUP-03/05/06 "would allow linking active preference" assumes that current register entries establish preferential eligibility; they establish potentially relevant supplier records, not necessarily the origin qualification of this shipment.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may be valid but unsupported by the supplied packet: the shipment could have been sourced from SUP-03, SUP-05 or SUP-06, with a valid declaration and governing rule held in Procurement archives. The missing supplier identifier and ClearView link therefore demonstrate a documentation and data-lineage control failure, not invalid origin or fraud. The United States manufacturing-country field likewise does not resolve preferential origin by itself.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State the applicable preferential-origin rule and evidence standard explicitly, then test whether each potentially relevant supplier declaration covers P1006, the shipment date, the actual supplier route and the rule before treating its discovery as sufficient to clear the claim.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185 of 262 qcore_release_ts values are exactly 02:10:00" and "The SOP defines the routine target...but the extract has no timestamp for certificate/specification/deviation evidence availability." These claims are tied to specific files, fields, and SOP sections, with source-freshness counterevidence acknowledged.

"excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours." This is not fully traceable as stated because evidence-availability timestamps are explicitly missing; the metric appears to be a proxy but is labeled as evidence-to-release.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Headline cycle time of 1.5 days conflates physical receipt-to-release...with the SOP-mandated evidence-to-release standard." This separates the observed symptom from the governing process definition.
"Whether 02:10 is a real disposition time or extract default" followed by a proposed live QCore audit tests the key competing explanations.
"the observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact" is somewhat too definitive before the proposed validation is completed.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission labels claims High or Medium-High confidence and states that missing/index-pending COA may be source lag rather than confirmed release.
"A live portal check is required before alleging a control breach" appropriately links uncertainty to an operational decision.

The conclusion that 02:10 is an artifact and that HOLD rows are "likely to become the slowest observations" is stronger than the available evidence warrants; both should remain conditional pending validation and follow-up.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer KPI dashboard publication pending timestamp verification." This directly reframes the task around whether the KPI is valid rather than optimizing an invalid measure.
The proposed read-only validation of 5–10 rows, plus evidence-field mapping and right-censoring analysis, is small, reversible, and operationally safe.
The recommendation protects against publishing a misleading KPI while defining conditions under which publication could resume.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission rejects "The data is broken and should be discarded" using populated fields and nonnegative durations, rejects treating 45.5 hours as the SOP cycle time using the SOP start definition, and rejects treating COA MISSING as proof of a control breach because of freshness lag.
The table explicitly states what evidence would revive each competing interpretation, including live QCore timestamps, CertVault reconciliation, and eventual HOLD outcomes.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Do one read-only validation of 5–10 02:10-stamped batches in live QCore and CertVault before building a dashboard" is a prioritized, minimal query with clear discriminatory value.
The submission also requests a validated evidence-availability field mapping for 5–10 batches and identifies how each result would change the decision.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is mislabeled or unsupported because the submission also states that evidence_available_ts is absent; it should be called a clearly defined proxy, likely lab-complete-to-release or another available timestamp measure.
"the observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact" is an inference, not yet an established fact; the proposed live audit is still needed.

"those [42 HOLD] rows...are likely to become the slowest observations" is plausible given their recency and open status but not demonstrated; completed-only bias should be described as likely or bounded rather than certain.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 timestamps may reflect genuine disposition times for at least some batches, while the apparent KPI problem could primarily be the missing evidence-availability event rather than a timestamp interface artifact. A live QCore audit sampling both 02:10-stamped and non-02:10 rows would discriminate these explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Correctly label the 8.4-hour statistic as an available-field proxy or remove it, then define and validate the exact event semantics for evidence availability and disposition using a small paired QCore/CertVault sample before presenting any cycle-time estimate.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The 24 open requests total $166,495.60..." citing `part_requests.csv`, all 24 rows, `qty`, `external_quote_usd`, and `status=OPEN`.
"Revision-B valve supply is two free units..." citing `spare_parts.csv`, `part_requests.csv`, and `part_restrictions.csv`.

The submission identifies relevant files, fields, request IDs, quantities, revisions, UOMs, reservations, and freshness dates; however, it does not provide row-level identifiers for every classification and presents the $20.5k as a firm saving despite stale global stock evidence.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Every search hit represents a direct transfer opportunity": rejected" using reserved MTR-4401 stock and zero stock at HA-0002.
"Same part family means interchangeable": rejected" using the revision-A versus revision-B valve conflict and policy approval requirements.

The analysis separates semantic candidate retrieval from transfer eligibility and tests alternatives involving reservations, revision parity, negative availability, and data hygiene; it could better test whether exact-MPN coverage actually eliminates the incremental value of semantic search for the 11 requests lacking identifiers.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "local CMMS is live, so ‘actionable now’ still requires current confirmation."
"Needs check" and "Not transferable on current evidence" appropriately distinguish unresolved from currently restricted cases.

The submission recognizes the 26 June MaintStar versus 24 July ProcureNet timing mismatch, but the headline classification and statement that the "firm saving is $20.5k" overstate certainty until live availability, reservation, and allocation checks are completed.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Treat search results as candidates, not automatic transfers."
"Test data hygiene and exact matching first."

The recommendation is operationally safer than automatic transfer and gives a prioritized path through exact matches, identity gaps, reservation checks, and revision approvals; it would be stronger with a small reversible pilot, explicit success criteria, and a quantified distinction between candidate value and confirmed actionable value.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects automatic transfer, family-level interchangeability, interpreting -1 availability as zero, and the claim that an expensive semantic-search system is necessarily required.

Each rejected hypothesis is tied to specific requests, locations, revisions, reservations, or the maintenance email, and the MTR conclusion is appropriately left open if records are wrong; it does not fully state what evidence would revive the broader semantic-search hypothesis beyond a general recall/precision comparison.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Manufacturer part number and revision from maintenance records" for the 11 blank-part-number requests.
"Live local CMMS reservation and availability query" for negative or stale stock.
"Receiving engineer and qualification approval" for revision substitutions.

The requested evidence is specific and decision-linked, but the submission does not prioritize which query should be run first by expected value or state the operational threshold for moving a candidate into an approved transfer.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The firm saving is $20.5k across 8 requests" is too strong while the global stock snapshot is stale and the submission itself says live confirmation is required; this is better described as provisional candidate value.

"Semantic search is not the real problem" and "Master-data hygiene, not search, is the priority" are not fully established by exact matches for the 13 requests that already have MPNs, because semantic search may still add value for the 11 requests with missing identifiers or for synonym and description normalization.
The "Actionable now" classifications remain provisional rather than confirmed transfers because availability, reservations, and allocation may have changed since the MaintStar extract.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Exact MPN matching is highly effective for the identified subset, but semantic search may still be valuable as a candidate-generation layer for the 11 requests without MPNs and for descriptions whose identifiers are absent or unreliable. The best conclusion is therefore not that semantic search is unnecessary, but that it should be evaluated against an exact-MPN baseline and coupled with engineering, revision, UOM, reservation, and live-availability confirmation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a prioritized live CMMS reconciliation for the eight provisional actionable requests and the negative-availability/competing-allocation cases, recording current free quantity, reservation status, revision, UOM, and qualification. Recast the resulting confirmed amount as actionable value, then run a small exact-MPN-versus-semantic pilot on the 11 unidentified requests with recall, precision, and confirmed-transfer yield as success criteria.
